relevance_reason: Reports a fetus with a skeletal ciliopathy phenotype (cleft lip/palate, pre- and postaxial polydactyly) and compound heterozygous RAB34 variants, which is the defining gene for OFD20.

findings.statement: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) reported a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype. The fetus had multiple malformations: posterior neck edema, micrognathia, low-set and small ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and a combination of preaxial and postaxial polydactyly, which rarely occur together.
quotes: The affected fetus had multiple malformations, including posterior neck edema, micrognathia, low-set and small ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and a combination of rarely occurring pre- and postaxial polydactyly.

findings.statement: In a fetus with a skeletal ciliopathy phenotype, Batkovskyte et al. (2024) identified compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene by genome sequencing: a maternally inherited missense variant, c.254T>C (p.Ile85Thr), and a paternally inherited nonsense variant, c.691C>T (p.Arg231Ter). Only the paternal variant was present in the unaffected sibling. The authors noted that Rab34-null mice display a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, supporting pathogenicity, and suggested RAB34 as a candidate gene for skeletal ciliopathies.
quotes: Genome sequencing identified compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene: maternal c.254T>C, p.(Ile85Thr), and paternal c.691C>T, p.(Arg231*) variants.
Only the paternal variant was present in the unaffected sibling.
suggests RAB34 as a candidate gene for skeletal ciliopathies

findings.statement: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) cited evidence from the literature that Rab34-null mice display a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, features consistent with those in their patient.
quotes: Evidence in the literature indicated that Rab34-/- mice displayed a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly.

relevance_reason: This is the original report of biallelic RAB34 variants causing a new type of oral-facial-digital syndrome (OFDS-RAB34). It includes patients and functional studies.

findings.statement: Bruel et al. (2023) described OFDS-RAB34, a new form of oral-facial-digital syndrome caused by biallelic RAB34 variants. Along with oral-facial-digital features, it includes cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
quotes: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.

findings.statement: Bruel et al. (2023) reported 4 affected individuals from 3 unrelated families with a new form of oral-facial-digital syndrome. Besides defects of the face, oral cavity and digits, they had cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
quotes: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families.
Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.

findings.statement: In 4 individuals with oral-facial-digital syndrome from 3 unrelated families, Bruel et al. (2023) used exome sequencing to identify biallelic missense variants in the RAB34 gene. The variants clustered near the C terminus of RAB34. The abstract does not give the individual variants.
quotes: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families.
the protein products of these pathogenic variants, which are clustered near the RAB34 C-terminus, exhibit a strong loss of function

findings.statement: In functional studies, Bruel et al. (2023) found that the mutant RAB34 proteins showed strong loss of function. Some variants could still be recruited to the mother centriole, but cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly. RAB34 acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway, and the authors concluded that RAB34 is the first small GTPase involved in OFDS.
quotes: Although some variants retain the ability to be recruited to the mother centriole, cells expressing mutant RAB34 exhibit a significant defect in cilium assembly.
Unlike many genes required for cilium assembly, RAB34 acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway, in which nascent cilia begin to form in the cytoplasm.
our studies establish RAB34 as the first small GTPase involved in OFDS and reveal the distinct clinical manifestations caused by impairment of intracellular ciliogenesis
